item.title: What’s at Stake: Binghamton Mayoral Race
item.description: In New York City, the mayoral race has taken a dramatic turn, with former governor Andrew Cuomo attempting to close the gap against Democratic Socialist Zohran Mamdani. Despite being a newcomer to politics, Mamdani’s sudden rise has rocked the New York City political landscape, as voters ponder the possibility of a Democratic Socialist for New York City Mayor.

item.title: Turning Back The Planet’s Clock
item.description: Climate Change is an extremely complicated problem. The Earth is an extremely delicate system—it has many layers and each of them interact with the others in ways we are still not completely sure about. This means that, when there is an imbalance, even a small one, it creates a huge change in the planet's weather, temperature, and biological systems.

item.title: Evangelical Christianity and American State Ideology: A Historical Review
item.description: When the 13 colonies were established throughout the 16th-18th centuries, the myriad Christian denominations that found themselves in the New World began integrating religious practices into the laws of their respective colonies.

item.title: The end of politics? A brief analysis of Türkiye in the context of competitive authoritarianism
item.description: In recent years, Türkiye's political trajectory has become one of the most debated cases in comparative politics due to its rapid transformation from a democratically promising EU candidate to an increasingly authoritarian system. Academics, policymakers, and international observers have highlighted Türkiye as a critical example of how elected governments can gradually erode democratic institutions while maintaining formal electoral procedures.

item.title: A Longstanding Program in Danger: The History of the US SNAP Program
item.description: The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) is the United States’ largest program aimed at combating hunger. However, it is currently under attack by the Trump administration, and millions of Americans are at risk of their welfare benefits being cut.

item.title: The Electoral College and Antimajoritarianism
item.description: The United States prides itself on democratic and egalitarian values. Despite this, we choose to elect our executive by means of an Electoral College, which due to its nature, sometimes produces antimajoritarian election outcomes. These results go against the wishes of a majority of voters.

item.title: The Story of Populist Rhetoric and Image in the Age of Information
item.description: “Eat the Rich.” “Power to the People.” “Make America Great Again.” These populist slogans pop up everywhere, from graffiti under an overpass to TikTok “For You” pages. item.title: Trump Administration Opens Arctic Wildlife Refuge to Oil Drilling
item.description: Trump announced in October that he would open the entire 1.56 million acres of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge's Coastal Plain to oil and gas leasing. These lands are sacred to the Gwich'in Nation, home to irreplaceable wildlife, wilderness, and cultural values, and have never seen industrialization.

item.description: Donald Trump promised supporters that the United States would make a show of strength by forcibly removing foreign nationals from the country by any means necessary and by putting an end to “unfair” trade deals that benefited foreign countries more than the US. item.title: Cooperation and Contention: The Dynamic Relationship Between the United States and China
item.description: The United States and China have one of the world’s most complex relationships. The two countries have experienced periods of tension and cooperation over a range of issues. Key areas of conflict between the two include trade and economic practices. While the US and China have a critical trade relationship, they are also major competitors.
